A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RIZE work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A and B are readable and support comparison across the reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original five-seed MuJoCo experiments with three and ten demonstrations, regularization ablations, reward dynamics, and hyperparameter sweeps.

after.justification: V2 retains original MuJoCo results and adds a distributional-versus-Q-critic ablation and comparative reward/value diagnostics.

M1.justification: RIZE retains the distributional critic, adaptive-target regularizer, SAC updates, and value/v0 loss variants. V2 makes entropy weighting and separate target learning rates explicit in the main equations/pseudocode, consistent with v1's SAC update and appendix settings; its expanded architecture description does not establish a new procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use HalfCheetah-v2, Walker2d-v2, Ant-v2, and Humanoid-v2 with SAC expert demonstrations. The new critic comparisons use these existing tasks without adding a domain, population, or environmental scenario.

E2.justification: The headline IQ-Learn, LSIQ, and SQIL comparator set is retained. V2 adds these baselines to the recovered-reward comparison, previously restricted to RIZE, and reports comparative critic-value diagnostics. Figure 5 additionally compares RIZE against its point-estimate-critic variant.

E3.justification: V2 adds a controlled distributional-versus-point-estimate critic experiment using three demonstrations and critic-value diagnostics using ten. Existing benchmark settings, expert-return normalization, training horizons, and listed hyperparameter values remain consistent across versions.

E4.justification: V2 Section 5.3 adds a direct test of the distributional critic's contribution across all four tasks, alongside comparative reward and critic-value analyses. Conversely, v1's three-demonstration reward traces and explicit adaptive-target trajectories are removed. The Ant regularization ablation and target, regularization-coefficient, and entropy sweeps are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five seeds and report means with half a standard deviation, including the hyperparameter analyses. V2 retains this uncertainty-reporting practice and introduces no new statistical test or estimation procedure.

E6.justification: New results in v2 Figures 3–5 show baseline reward/value dynamics and the point-estimate critic's failure to reach expert-level Humanoid performance. The critic diagnostics show sharply growing Humanoid values for IQ-Learn/SQIL, unlike RIZE/LSIQ. Some earlier reward/target result entries disappear; headline performance findings and retained sensitivity trends remain similar.

T1.justification: V1 Lemma 4.1 derives a convex-combination reward bound by optimizing the regularizer alone. V2 Proposition 4.1 differentiates the full objective, adding an occupancy-difference term and expanding the bounds by 1/(2c); Appendix A also derives an occupancy-matching equilibrium. The temporal-consistency argument is removed, and the soft-return expectation lemma drops the earlier DCT-based learned-distribution convergence claim.

C1.justification: The adaptive-target/distributional-IRL contribution and expert-level Humanoid performance with three demonstrations remain central. V2 explicitly foregrounds derived adaptive reward bounds and newly claims that both adaptive rewards and distributional learning are essential for Humanoid, extending v1's contribution statements.

C2.justification: V2 distinguishes bounded critics from successful imitation, using LSIQ as a counterexample, and interprets baseline reward/value instability. Section 4.2 newly acknowledges that IQ-Learn's convergence guarantee does not cover the practical chi-squared regularizer and that alternating SAC convergence remains unproved, materially qualifying the stability discussion.

D1.justification: V2 Appendix B.1 newly identifies IQ-Learn as the source of the SAC expert trajectories. Algorithm 1 clarifies separate target learning-rate symbols, and the table corrects the policy-target learning-rate heading. The underlying architecture, hyperparameter values, and code-access information were already provided in v1.

R1.justification: V2 broadens the introduction with sparse-reward, preference-learning, and intrinsic-motivation literature, adds Muller et al. (2024) as distributional-learning motivation, and cites Viano et al. (2022) on convergence limitations. Mnih et al. (2015) is removed. The central positioning relative to IQ-Learn, LSIQ, and SQIL remains.

P1.justification: The introduction and methodology are substantially rewritten and resequenced, including moving expectation and target-update equations into earlier subsections. Extended performance material is integrated into the main narrative, appendix subsections are consolidated, and unresolved Figure X, Equations X, and Reference X placeholders are removed or replaced.

P2.justification: V2 redraws and compresses plots, revises legends and colors, moves v1's combined demonstration-count performance plot into the main text, and adds reward/value grids and the critic ablation. Target-trajectory plots disappear, two hyperparameter tables become one, and separate coefficient-sensitivity figures become paired panels.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses two important weaknesses: Proposition 4.1 analyzes the full reward objective, correcting v1's regularizer-only argument, and Figure 5 directly tests the distributional critic's contribution. The explicit convergence limitation also improves claim calibration. These substantial gains in the central justification outweigh the loss of some reward and adaptive-target diagnostics.
